event.name: 7 September 1999 Athens (Attica), Greece, earthquake
event.tectonic_setting: Thriassion basin–Parnitha/Fili fault system, Attica; normal faulting along an approximately ESE–WNW plane.

reference.title: Postseismic displacement of the 1999 Athens earthquake retrieved by the Differential Interferometry by Synthetic Aperture Radar time series
reference.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth, 113, B09309

inversion.method: Coseismic ascending and descending ERS-1/2 DInSAR time-series displacement joint linear inversion; fault geometry estimated with nonlinear inversion, then fixed for 20 x 20 patch linear nonnegative least squares inversion with Laplacian smoothing. Model is the COSEISMIC Figure 4, NOT the postseismic afterslip Figure 7.
inversion.green_function_model: Okada (1985) dislocations in a homogeneous elastic half-space; strike 110°, dip 60°, rake -80°.
inversion.notes: CATEGORY DIGITIZATION of published Atzori et al. (2008) Figure 4 (PDF p. 5), not the numerical inversion output. The geocoded map shows a tilted ground-projection of a 20x20 fault grid: 20 along-strike cells of 1.75 km and 20 downdip cells of 1.25 km. Cell classes 0, 0-10, 10-20,...,80-90 cm were read from printed legend after perspective rectification and exclusion of relief, hatching and grid-line pixels; each nonzero cell stores the interval midpoint rather than an exact measured slip. All 400 original mesh cells are included; 353 hatched cells are zero and 47 classified colored cells occupy 102.8125 km2, agreeing with the paper (47 coseismic patches; 102.8 km2). The paper reports peak slip ~0.8 m at ~8.5 km and geodetic moment 0.78e18 Nm; sampled 80-90 cm categories have assigned midpoint 0.85 m, not an independently resolved peak. The mean midpoint slip is 0.03063 m over all 400 cells, or 0.26064 m when restricted to 47 colored cells; neither is an author-reported mean. The absolute top-depth datum for the full extended 20x20 plane is not tabulated; top_depth_km=0.86 is an approximate reference inferred from the paper's mention of a shallow top active patch, and calculated patch depths are consequently approximate. The source gives several alternative hypocentres; event.hypocenter uses the USGS-NEIC solution from Table 2 (38.02 N, 23.55 E, 9 km). Slip-patch geographical coordinates remain null because a trustworthy full-plane georeferencing anchor is not given. Event origin time follows the 1999 Athens mainshock catalogue epoch, while the model belongs specifically to the coseismic phase; Atzori et al. also publish a separate afterslip model.

provenance.compiled_by: Visual reconstruction of published categorical slip map; rectified original 20x20 mesh, sampled published nine-class colorbar; per-cell audit CSV and QA figure included.
